brief.headline: Warburg Pincus Lifts Ingenia Bid to $1.6B, Ramping Up Bidding War With Brookfield
bullets: Macro & Geopolitics: Warburg Pincus has raised its takeover offer for Ingenia Communities Group for a third time, topping a rival bid from a group led by Brookfield and local player Avid Property Group.
Private Credit: KKR has closed its first private credit continuation vehicle with more than $460 million of total commitments, PitchBook reported, citing market sources.
M&A & Buyouts: The Korean government has ended its eight-year legal fight with Elliott Management over the 2015 merger of Samsung C T and Cheil Industries.
AI & Technology: They also discuss how they built one of the most influential media companies of the last decade and lessons from their new book, Simplify: Do 50% More with 50% Less.
Fundraising: ACORE Capital has closed its second opportunistic real estate credit fund at $1.1bn (£820m), exceeding its original $1bn fundraising target.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,743.98 (up 0.3% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 16.9, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.99% (down 1 bp on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.38 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.14%, near long-run norms (down 4 bps on the prior reading).

items.title: KKR Closed Its First Private Credit Continuation Vehicle at More Than $460 Million, With AllianzGI Leading
items.takeaway: KKR has closed its first private credit continuation vehicle with more than $460 million of total commitments, PitchBook reported, citing market sources.
items.whyItMatters: Continuation funds let managers keep their best assets longer while giving existing investors a way out, so the key question for investors is whether the price is fair.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.14%, near long-run norms (down 4 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Oct 28.)

beginnerNote.explanation: A new fund set up by a manager to keep holding its best assets longer, while giving existing investors the option to cash out.

items.title: ACORE Capital closes second opportunistic credit fund at $1.1bn
items.takeaway: ACORE Capital has closed its second opportunistic real estate credit fund at $1.1bn (£820m), exceeding its original $1bn fundraising target.
items.whyItMatters: ACORE Capital's $1.1bn raise shows investors are still committing money to real estate, and a strong raise makes it easier for other managers in the strategy to raise too.
items.marketContext: The S&P 500 stands at 7,743.98 (up 0.3% on the prior reading) and the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.99% (down 1 bp on the prior reading). Stock and bond levels change how much room investors have for private assets. When public holdings fall, private allocations look overweight (the "denominator effect"). (FRED data as of Oct 28.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Money investors have committed to private funds that has not yet been invested. It is a measure of how much buying power is waiting on the sidelines.

items.title: Silverstreak provides $20m private credit facility to Fingular
items.takeaway: Singapore-based private credit firm Silverstreak Group has provided a $20m (£15m) credit facility to fintech group Fingular to support the expansion of its lending operations in Malaysia.
items.whyItMatters: This $20m deal shows private lenders are still putting money to work in private credit, and the terms they win set the bar for returns across the strategy.
